report.evidence: Review round 1 (Faro, 8f5530a) findings addressed. Finding 1: grant needs an interactive TTY plus a typed confirmation of '<grantee> <scopes>'. grant and revoke refuse AO_AGENT_ID, TM_SESSION_ID, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CODEX_* and a tmux pane the census binds to an agent. Grants record channel evidence and an assurance field stating a same-OS-user agent is NOT excluded. Events are HMAC-signed (mode-600 key), and integrate/record-landing refuse a file with any unsigned, edited or evidence-less event. Finding 2: under a delegation, authorization.actor = grantee (the caller's AO_AGENT_ID), with delegated_by and delegation_id alongside. A differing --actor is refused with TOPOLOGY_DELEGATION_ACTOR in both integrate and record-landing, and tests assert both.
risks: A deliberate agent running as the same OS user can still forge a grant: it can unset the markers, drive a pty (script or tmux send-keys) and read the mode-600 key. This is documented and recorded in each grant's assurance field. Full exclusion needs a different-uid key holder or the session-host capability channel, which is out of scope here.
Round-1 grant records (no mac or channel) are now refused. Any existing delegations file must be re-granted.
Toward the approved plan-approval work: record-landing no longer needs --actor under a delegation, so refusing --actor inside managed sessions later is a one-line change.

report.evidence: Addresses Faro's round-1 review of 8f5530a. The lead (d60f0608) narrowed the fix. FINDING 1 (grant channel): grant refuses any agent marker (AO_AGENT_ID, TM_SESSION_ID, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CODEX_*), a Claude Code or Codex ancestor process, and a tmux pane the census binds to an agent. It also requires an interactive TTY and a typed confirmation '<grantee> <scopes>'. revoke has the same refusals, without the confirmation. The grant records the checks it passed as channel evidence: kind 'interactive-same-user', agent_proof false, and a note that it is not agent-proof against a same-uid agent, which can drive a TTY through tmux or script. integrate and record-landing refuse a delegations file holding any grant without that evidence. HMAC signing was deliberately dropped: the key would be readable by the same uid, so a signature added nothing and would have looked like proof. repository-leads.md says all of this and names a different-uid grant store or a session-host capability channel as future work. That architecture decision belongs to the marketplace lead and the operator. FINDING 2 (actor): under a delegation, authorization.actor is the grantee (the caller's AO_AGENT_ID), with delegated_by and delegation_id alongside. integrate and record-landing refuse an --actor that differs from the grantee (TOPOLOGY_DELEGATION_ACTOR), and tests assert both.
risks: NOT agent-proof against a same-OS-user agent. Such an agent can unset the markers, start a shell outside its own process tree, drive a TTY through tmux or script, or write the delegations file directly with copied evidence fields. The checks stop ordinary-path use only. This is stated in every grant and in the docs.
Grants made by round-1 code carry no channel evidence and are now refused, so any existing grant must be re-granted.
Toward the approved plan-approval work: record-landing no longer needs --actor under a delegation, so refusing --actor inside managed sessions later is a one-line change.
